content.text:
This confirms: `getRunningBatchKey()` (public, exposed via interface) was introduced in c9e5d87, and the same commit wired it into `VariablesFactory.createVariables()` — a method invoked on essentially every variable resolution, including scenario/examples-table parsing that jbehave-junit-runner performs while building its JUnit `Description` tree, i.e., before `BatchedEmbedder.putRunningBatch()` is ever called. Since the underlying field `runningBatchKey` has been uninitialized (`null`, not `Optional.empty()`) ever since the class was created, this new early-invoked call path hit a `NullPointerException` calling `.orElseThrow()` on `null`, instead of the intended `IllegalStateException`.

Let me double check whether `a1e05bf` (AllureStoryReporter) could independently trigger this under jbehave-junit-runner, and check the VariablesFactoryTests/story integration test added in c9e5d87 for further confirmation of intent.

content.text:
This confirms my hypothesis: I have enough evidence to conclude.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: c9e5d87268285bf5a3016cbb688e12a19fba0858

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `BddRunContext.java`, focused by the fix's own comment ("must be initialized for jbehave-junit-runner") and the field `runningBatchKey`. `git log --follow -p` showed this field has been declared without an initializer (`private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;`) since the class was first created in `aef6f032` (Aug 2019) — that alone is a latent gap, but harmless as long as nothing reads it before `putRunningBatch()` runs. I then searched for all call sites of the newly-exposed `getRunningBatchKey()` method and found two commits that introduced new callers: `c9e5d87` (added a call inside `VariablesFactory.createVariables()`) and `a1e05bf` (added a call inside `AllureStoryReporter.beforeStory()`).

**(2) The specific change:** `c9e5d87268285bf5a3016cbb688e12a19fba0858` ("batch-scoped variables" feature) did three things together:
 - Exposed `getRunningBatchKey()` on `IBddRunContext`/`BddRunContext` (previously the key was only used internally inside `getRunningBatch()`).
 - Wired it into `VariablesFactory.createVariables()`: `globalScoped.putAll(batchVariables.getOrDefault(bddRunContext.getRunningBatchKey(), Map.of()))`.
 - `createVariables()` is invoked from `BddVariableContext.getVariables()` essentially any time a variable/placeholder is resolved (e.g. story/scenario meta and Examples-table placeholders), not just during actual story execution.

Under the normal Vividus/Gradle run path (`BatchedEmbedder.runStoriesAsPaths`), `putRunningBatch()` is always called before any stories are parsed/run, so `runningBatchKey` is populated by the time `getRunningBatchKey()` is called. But `jbehave-junit-runner` builds its JUnit `Description` tree by parsing/resolving story structure (including Examples tables, which need variable resolution for parameterized scenario names) independently of `BatchedEmbedder.runStoriesAsPaths()`, i.e. before `putRunningBatch()` is ever invoked. In that path, `runningBatchKey` is still `null` (not `Optional.empty()`), so `runningBatchKey.orElseThrow(...)` threw an uncaught `NullPointerException` instead of the intended, informative `IllegalStateException` — breaking JUnit-runner-based test discovery.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit's own comment — "must be initialized for jbehave-junit-runner" — and its default value `Optional.of("batch-1")` directly address this early-access scenario. `git show c9e5d87` shows this commit is exactly where `getRunningBatchKey()` first became reachable from generic variable resolution (`VariablesFactory.createVariables()`), which is the mechanism jbehave-junit-runner relies on to resolve Examples-table placeholders while building its description tree, ahead of the batch actually starting.

I also considered `a1e05bf` (which added a similar call in `AllureStoryReporter.beforeStory()`), but that call only fires as a `StoryReporter` callback during actual story execution via `storyManager.runStoriesAsPaths()` — which always happens after `putRunningBatch()` in `BatchedEmbedder`, so it's unlikely to be reached by jbehave-junit-runner's pre-execution description-building phase. I have moderate-high but not absolute confidence, since I cannot execute jbehave-junit-runner locally (no network/build access) to directly reproduce the NPE and rule out `a1e05bf` with certainty.
